headline_marked: 11 balls for 50: [[Vaibhav Suryavanshi sets world record]] in List A cricket
headline: 11 balls for 50: Vaibhav Suryavanshi sets world record in List A cricket
summary: The 15-year-old Indian prodigy smashed a half-century in just 11 balls during a tri-series final against Sri Lanka 'A'.
details: Indian teenage sensation Vaibhav Suryavanshi has set a new world record for the fastest fifty in 50-over (List A) cricket, reaching the milestone in just 11 balls.
The record-breaking feat occurred during the final of a tri-series in Dambulla, where Suryavanshi played for India 'A' against Sri Lanka 'A'.
Suryavanshi broke the previous record held by Sri Lankan player Kaushal Veeraratne, who scored a fifty in 12 balls back in 2005.
The 15-year-old's explosive batting display included 10 boundaries in his first 11 balls, featuring 5 sixes.
He continued his aggressive approach, eventually scoring 94 runs off 29 balls before being caught at mid-off off the bowling of Sahan Arachchige.
His final tally of 94 runs included a total of 10 fours and 8 sixes, nearly reaching a century in a remarkably short span of time.
caption:
A 15-year-old just rewrote the cricket record books! 🏏

Indian teenage sensation Vaibhav Suryavanshi has set a new world record for the fastest fifty in 50-over (List A) cricket, reaching the milestone in just 11 balls.

The record-breaking feat occurred during the final of a tri-series in Dambulla, where Suryavanshi played for India 'A' against Sri Lanka 'A'.

Suryavanshi broke the previous record held by Sri Lankan player Kaushal Veeraratne, who scored a fifty in 12 balls back in 2005.

The 15-year-old's explosive batting display included 10 boundaries in his first 11 balls, featuring 5 sixes.

He continued his aggressive approach, eventually scoring 94 runs off 29 balls before being caught at mid-off off the bowling of Sahan Arachchige.

His final tally of 94 runs included a total of 10 fours and 8 sixes, nearly reaching a century in a remarkably short span of time.

headline_marked: Reports: [[UK PM Keir Starmer ready to quit]], but government sources deny
headline: Reports: UK PM Keir Starmer ready to quit, but government sources deny
summary: The Observer reports Starmer may resign tomorrow, amid growing pressure from within the Labour party and a recent parliamentary win by rival Andy Burnham.
details: Britain's The Observer newspaper reports that Prime Minister Keir Starmer is expected to resign tomorrow and set out a timetable for his departure.
A government source, however, has denied these reports, stating that Starmer remains focused on the job of governing the country.
The pressure on Starmer's position has increased following a parliamentary seat win by his rival, Andy Burnham, which allows Burnham to launch a formal leadership challenge.
Over 100 Labour lawmakers—roughly a quarter of the party's representatives in the House of Commons—have publicly called for his exit or a timetable for his departure.
Starmer has faced deep unpopularity due to a series of scandals and policy u-turns, with voters feeling he has failed to deliver promised improvements to living standards.
If he were to quit or be ousted, the UK would have its seventh prime minister in just over a decade, reflecting a period of high political instability.
Andy Burnham, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, is seen as the most likely successor, with some reports suggesting he would replace finance minister Rachel Reeves if he took power.
Starmer has vowed to fight any challenge to his leadership and has urged his party not to tear itself apart with internal infighting.
caption:
Is the UK Prime Minister stepping down? Reports suggest Keir Starmer is ready to quit, though his government denies it.

Britain's The Observer newspaper reports that Prime Minister Keir Starmer is expected to resign tomorrow and set out a timetable for his departure.

A government source, however, has denied these reports, stating that Starmer remains focused on the job of governing the country.

The pressure on Starmer's position has increased following a parliamentary seat win by his rival, Andy Burnham, which allows Burnham to launch a formal leadership challenge.

Over 100 Labour lawmakers—roughly a quarter of the party's representatives in the House of Commons—have publicly called for his exit or a timetable for his departure.

Starmer has faced deep unpopularity due to a series of scandals and policy u-turns, with voters feeling he has failed to deliver promised improvements to living standards.

If he were to quit or be ousted, the UK would have its seventh prime minister in just over a decade, reflecting a period of high political instability.

Andy Burnham, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, is seen as the most likely successor, with some reports suggesting he would replace finance minister Rachel Reeves if he took power.

Starmer has vowed to fight any challenge to his leadership and has urged his party not to tear itself apart with internal infighting.
